normalized.title: TWELFTH FIXED CALL FOR PROPOSALS UNDER THE PLAN FOR EUROPEAN COOPERATING STATES (PECS) IN BULGARIA
normalized.description: The European Space Agency and the Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation of the Republic of Bulgaria hereby invite you to submit a proposal for the above Call for Proposals, which will be soon published in esa-star. While it is made visible to all ESA Member States, Associate Members and European Cooperating States, this CfP will be addressed only to Bulgarian legal entities registered in ESA-STAR, as prime tenderer and foresees the following standard activity types: Type A Research and Preparatory Activities, aimed at the preparation for participation in ESA optional programmes or the initial steps of a product development for Space, with potential for use on future ESA missions or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 1 and the target TRL shall be TRL3 or below. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 200,000. Type B Flight- and Ground Segment-related Research and Development Activities, targetting equipment to build competences and capabilities centred on products or generic technology development with potential for re-use on ESA or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 3 and the target TRL shall be TRL 6. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 500,000 (hardware development)/EUR 250,000 (all other activities). Type D Space science activities, supporting the involvement of national researchers leading to potential of future involvement in ESA science mission core team and publication of peer reviewed scientific papers. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 75,000.Type E: Phase 0/A/B1 small sat mission definition studies with potential to lead to either a national or a commercial mission, in the area of Earth Observation for Climate, Agriculture, Disaster Management and Environmental Monitoring, enabling the development and demonstration of Bulgarian technologies and products in space. Maximum price for ESA 300.000 Euros. Type F Space Applications, products and services making use of ESA/ European space infrastructure that is already existing or scheduled for operation in the near term. The start TRL shall be at least 6 and the target TRL shall be TRL 8. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 200,000. The work carried out by the Tenderer must be co-funded to a minimum level of 25% of the total cost of the activity. Type G1 University courses/modules leading to a qualification (BSc or MSc) in space related topics that correspond to the needs of national space industry and to encourage career in space and answer to national space industry needs. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 70,000. To be published as a separate tender in esa-star: Type G2 PhD Theses that correspond to a clear need from the national space industry and would lead to a new product or service being able to be developed. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 75,000 with a minimum company co-funding of EUR 10,000. More information and further programmatic constraints can be consulted in the cover letter of the call upon its issue date.

normalized.title: INCUBED-2 STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSAL
normalized.description: The InCubed Element of the European Earth Watch Programme (InCubed) aims at accompanying the European economic operators in the Earth Observation market rapid evolution currently witnessed in Europe and overseas. InCubed offers a new process in ESA Earth Observation programmes to strengthen and stimulate the realization of endeavours near-to-the-market with Economic Operators. Activities to be supported include the development and/or demonstration of space assets (missions, instruments, prototype element of EO constellation), innovative mission management solution, including for future EO constellation, the development of application platforms, etc. InCubed is looking for commercial viability by the end of the activity (up to at least a minimum viable product level) and a substantial degree of innovation i.e. adding new value to the EO commercial landscape. Commercial customer engagement/involvement is mandatory. Commercial customers are encouraged to be either as part of the consortium representing the value chain or as beta testers/validators of the developed product/service.  Customer engagement/involvement must be highlighted at the pitch and proposal stage. Letters of potential customer support/interest are seen as a very positive aspect. The actual scope of the proposed activities is defined by the economic operators themselves in relevance to the InCubed objectives. Two development cycles are possible within InCubed: TheDe-Risking Cycle (start TRL 4) and Product Development Cycle (startTRL 6) depending on the maturity of the concept being developed. Regarding this forthcoming Announcement of Partnership Opportunity, Economic operators are invited to register and submit idea pitches onto ideas.esa.int (InCubed channel). Following a positive pitch meeting, the second step is to fill in a Part 1 (Outline) proposal template, which must be supported by the Participating State(s) having jurisdiction over them. Following a positive assessment,the economic operators will be invited to submit a Part 2 (Full) proposal template, as per established procedure and evaluation criteria. The proposals to be supported by InCubed will have to be co-funded by the economic operators (partnership agreements), as a sign of their engagement and belief in their own business case.

normalized.title: INCUBED CALL FOR PROPOSAL: STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSALS
normalized.description: The InCubed Element of the European Earth Watch Programme (InCubed) aims to accompany European economic operators in the rapid evolution of the Earth Observation market, both in Europe and globally. InCubed introduces a dedicated process within ESA Earth Observation programmes to strengthen and stimulate the development of near-to-market commercial initiatives in partnership with industry. Activities supported under InCubed include the development and/or demonstration of space assets (e.g. missions, instruments, prototype elements of EO constellations), innovative mission management solutions (including for future EO constellations), as well as the development of ground, data, and application platforms. InCubed targets commercial viability by the end of the activity (at least at minimum viable product level) and requires a substantial degree of innovation, i.e. the creation of new value within the EO commercial landscape. Commercial customer engagement is mandatory, with customers acting as beta testers and validators of the developed product or service. Customer engagement must be clearly demonstrated at both pitch and proposal stages, and letters of support or interest from potential customers are considered a strong asset. The scope of the proposed activities is defined by the economic operators themselves, in line with the objectives of InCubed. Two development cycles are available within InCubed, depending on the maturity of the concept: De-risking Cycle (typically starting from TRL 4), focusing on reducing technical and market risks;Product Development Cycle (typically starting from TRL 6), aiming at delivering a product ready for commercialisation. Under this Call for Proposals, economic operators are invited to submit their ideas via the OSIP (Open Space Innovation Platform) (ideas.esa.int), which serves as the entry point for the programme. The application process consists of the following step: Idea Pitch - Applicantssubmit and present a draft Outline proposal via OSIP to ESA (and potentially the relevant National Delegation(s)). Following a positive assessment, economic operators will be invited to submit a Proposal Part 2 (Full) in accordance with the established procedures and evaluation criteria. Activities supported under InCubed are based on a co-funding scheme, whereby economic operators contribute financially to the project, demonstrating commitment to and confidence in their business case.

normalized.description: The Luxembourg's National Programme - LuxIMPULSE Programme, aims to strengthen worldwide competitiveness of Luxembourg industry in the near term in existing markets and to establish strategic capabilities which will result in stronger competitiveness in the medium term on existing or new markets, and to support the implementation of Luxembourg national priorities.The Call for Proposals is addressed only to economic operators - be it as Prime or Subcontractor level - registered in Luxembourg, unless otherwise instructed and approved by the Luxembourg Space Agency. The economic operator's contribution can be either monetary or in-kind.

normalized.description: This procurement targets the delivery of the Copernicus Space Component acquisition services, including the Sentinels X-Band data acquisition operations and the S-band Telemetry, Tracking and Control (TTC) services.The X-Band Acquisition service aims at the on-ground reception of data sensed by the Sentinel satellites and the delivery of the acquired data in the form of CADU data stream for further ground segment operations. This procedure consists therefore in a two-step procurement approach, broken down as follows: Step 1 -Qualification Phase: The objective of this Step is to award, through an Open Competition Frame Contracts with the entities qualifying for the performance of the services subject of this procurement. Step 2 -Implementation Phase: The objective of this Step is to award, through Restricted Competitions between the Frame Contractors qualified under Step 1, the Work Orders allowing the performance of the procured services.An Information day about the subject procurement was organized at the European Space Agency (ESA) in December 2018. The location, date, registration process and Agenda of this briefing session was published on ESA Tendering website (EMITS) under "NEWS" (http://emits.sso.esa.int/emits/owa/emits.main). Potential bidders are invited to consult regularly ESA Tendering website (EMITS).The Acquisition And TTC Services For Copernicus procurements will be fundedby the Copernicus Programme and will be open exclusively to economic operators, which have their registered office in an EU Member State or Iceland or Norway.In order to access the Frame ITT Package from EMITS, any economic operator interested in the subject procurement will have to be registered as a potential ESA Tenderer. To register with ESA as a potential Tenderer, you will be requestedto complete the online questionnaire available ESA-STAR registration website: https://esastar-emr.sso.esa.int. While the registration process is underway, potential ESA Tenderers may access the Frame ITT Package through ESA's dedicated Copernicus server, which is accessible at: https://copernicus-emits.esa.int/

This procedure consists of a two-step procurement approach, broken down as follows:Step 1 - Open Qualification Period: The objective of this Step is to award, through an Open Competition (Frame ITT), Frame Contracts to several  Frame-Contractors  (Competitive Frame Contracts)Step 2 - Long Term Archive Service Implementation: The objective of this Step is to award the Work Orders through Restricted Competitions (RFP) between the Frame Contractors qualified under Step 1, allowing the implementation of the requested Long Term Archive Service.An Information day for this procurement will be held at ESRIN at 10:00am CEST on July 12th 2019. Further information on this briefing session has been published on ESA Tendering website (EMITS) under NEWS (http://emits.sso.esa.int/emits/owa/emits.main). Potential bidders are invited to consult regularly the ESA Tendering website. This Long Term Archive Service is funded by the Copernicus Programme and will be open exclusively to economic operators, that have their registered office in an EU Member State or Iceland or Norway. In order to access the Frame ITT Package from EMITS, any economic operator interested in the procurement will have to be registered as a potential ESA Tenderer. To register with ESA as a potential Tenderer, it is necessary to complete the online questionnaire available on the ESA-STAR registration website: https://esastar-emr.sso.esa.int. Whilst the registration process is underway, potential ESA Tenderers may access the Frame ITT Package through ESA's dedicated Copernicus server: https://copernicus-emits.esa.int/

Description:
The Contracting Authority is seeking tenders for the procurement of a High-Precision Optical Ground Station (OGS) Telescope Unit for Uplink and Satellite Tracking. This procurement is being undertaken as part of Phase 2 of Ireland's QCI project (TransEuroOGS), co-funded by the European Commission Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) and the Irish Department of Culture, Communications, and Sport. The successful tenderer will be required to design, manufacture, and deliver a turnkey telescope unit encompassing the mount, optics, and control software, complying with strict technical and spatial constraints. Key Technical Requirements: Optical Configuration: Ritchey-Chretien (RC) optical design, f/10 to f/12 system, with a clear aperture of at least 700 mm. Low central obstruction is required (30 percent or lower diameter linear obstruction preferred, maximum allowable 34 percent or lower). Optical Coatings and Power Handling: Broad-spectrum reflectivity covering both visible wavelengths and the 1550 nm C-Band NIR telecommunication spectrum, biased for optimal performance at 1550 nm. Reflectance at 1550 nm must be at least 95 percent (protected gold or equivalent high-efficiency NIR coating acceptable). The secondary mirror (M2) and main aperture must handle a high-power launch beam of maximum 40W continuous wave at 1550 nm across the aperture or annulus (power density less than 3300 W per square metre on the primary mirror). Focusing Path and Clear Aperture: Must feature at least one Nasmyth focus port (more preferred). The Nasmyth focus path must be completely free of refracting optical elements (100 percent reflective optics only, with removable optics as an allowable deviation). Clear aperture path through the Nasmyth axis must be at least 60 mm diameter to support downstream Adaptive Optics relay systems. Mount and Dynamic Tracking Specifications: Alt-Azimuth Direct-Drive or equivalent performance mount with low-latency tracking dynamics supporting Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite tracking, including high-elevation passes over Zenith. Minimum Azimuth Slew Rate must be at least 5 degrees per second (faster preferred). Pointing and tracking accuracy must be less than 8 to 10 arcsec RMS during dynamic LEO passes. Fastest tracking rate must exceed 1 degree per second with fine range control below this speed. Envelope and Enclosure Compatibility: Total vertical height must not exceed 3000 mm from the base to ensure dome clearance. Maximum radial swing clearance envelope must be at most 1470 mm. The axis of elevation pivot height must ensure clearance at all pointing directions, with the pivot axis positioned no more than 155 mm below the centre of the clearance envelope (or at the centre or higher). Full CAD models and opto-mechanical layout files are mandatory upon contract award. Software, Control Interface and API: Native integration with standard open-source astronomical communication protocols (INDI / INDIGO) or ASCOM / ALPACA frameworks. Open, fully documented network API adaptable to HTTP/REST or WebSocket interfaces for automated robotic control, telemetry, and scriptable trajectory loading. Ethernet data interface and DC power supply preferred. Delivery Constraint: Unit delivery must be completed within 3 to 4 months maximum from contract signature. Please refer to the detailed Technical Specification document for full technical specifications, compliance matrices, and contractual terms.

Digital Investment Facility (DIF) Local Coordinator for Connectivity for Central Asia (C4CA) programme HAUS Finnish Institute of Public Management Ltd is procuring a Central Asia-based Local Coordinator to support the establishment and operation of the Digital Investment Facility (DIF) under the EU-funded Connectivity for Central Asia (C4CA) programme. The assignment is expected to start in Q4/2026 and last approximately 12 months, with a home-based duty station in Central Asia.

DIF is designed as an advisory facility that helps last-mile connectivity projects (rural mobile coverage, suburban fibre and satellite backhaul) move towards investment readiness and connects them with European and international financiers. The Local Coordinator will map and engage ministries, regulators, telecom operators and project promoters in Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan, identify candidate projects, support the submission of Expressions of Interest and carry out first-level eligibility screening. The coordinator will also support the selection and preparation of 2–3 pilot projects for tailored technical assistance, contribute to adapting the DIF model and a regional PPP concept to the Central Asian context, and support investor engagement, including roundtables.

Further details are provided in Annex 1 (ToR).,
